omissions.reason: The canceled final x of French deux leaves deu; the English word two has no corresponding letter change.
A canceled stray x inside également has no English lexical effect.
A canceled stray x following général has no English lexical effect; the live uncertainty in the final French l remains marked in English.
The cancellation of s in the French determiner les leaves le; both determiners translate as the in this clause.
The cancellation of s in the French determiner les has no English lexical effect in the following phrase with inserted deux.
The canceled e before the apostrophe in qu’elles is a French elision correction without an English wording change.
The canceled stray x between faisceau and normal has no English effect; normal sheaf renders the surviving phrase.

variant_notes.note: The French plural s is canceled in critère(s). English expresses the same noun-number change by the full-word pair criteria/criterion; the variant therefore contains the whole English noun.
